messages:
Anya: Quick FYI — noticed a tail latency regression on prod-rt-4 starting ~03/12. Small but reproducible spike in rejected batches when KV cache utilization climbs above ~85%.

Kyle: Can you paste the logs/trace? Is this the OOM guard we added last quarter?

Anya: Yep, looks like the soft OOM guard admission path. Short thread of notes + raw logs below. This is specific to continuous batching: batch formation chooses larger token budgets, kernel selection cost jumps, then the KV headroom check rejects or shrinks the batch causing extra queue churn and higher p95.

Sam: Ugh — that pattern rings a bell. Bigger batches => more KV footprint per request due to longer prefixes/kvcache hits, but our headroom model assumes avg KV delta. If that delta is off, we mis-estimate and over-admit.

bench-bot: quick profile dump for the interval (03/12 14:10-14:20):
```
kernel_select          62.3%  (hot path: multihead mm, seq_len variance)
token_emit             17.9%
kv_mem_accounting      9.8%
admission_checks       6.4%  (includes OOM guard)
queue_management       3.6%
```

Anya: Raw OOM guard logs:
```
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] OOM_GUARD: reject_batch batch_id=0x7f8a reason=kv_headroom
 requested_tokens=32 admitted_tokens=16 kv_est_bytes=124MB headroom_needed=256MB node_free_kv=200MB
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] BATCHER: shrink batch_id=0x7f8a -> new_size=16 (requeue)
```

Kyle: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) kernel selection is picking an expensive kernel for the large batch window (e.g., full attention path vs optimized blocked-attn) due to seq_len estimate being wrong, increasing runtime memory pressure; (2) token budget target for continuous batching is too aggressive for workloads with high KV churn.

Sam: Agreed. Suggested short experiments: 1) Lower token_budget_target by 20% for the continuous-batcher canary. 2) Add a conservative KV async estimator that multiplies measured per-request KV delta by 1.5 before admission. 3) Add a micro-window cap (max batch token window 12ms) to reduce kernel-selection variance.

Anya: I ran a quick canary on a single node with token_budget -20% and the incidents dropped from ~6/hr to ~1/hr. Tail latency improved ~8ms p95. Kernel selection cost still high in some tails.

bench-bot: canary perf diff (node 7):
```
config: token_budget_target=0.8x (was 1.0x)
results: rejected_batches -83%, tail_latency_p95 -8ms, throughput -2.1%
hotspots: kernel_select still 48% in worst buckets
```

Kyle: The kernel_select hotspot suggests we should also add a lightweight preflight: before forming a large batch, sample the top-of-queue seq_len distribution and run the kernel route estimator (cheap heuristic) to pick expected kernel cost; if expected kernel cost crosses threshold, pre-limit the batch. This avoids committing to a heavy kernel at admission time.

Sam: Probably worth hooking that into the admission path as a fast path check (no locking) — just read the queue snapshot. Also add a kv_estimator smoothing window to avoid reacting to transient bursts.

Anya: Action items I propose:
- Kyle: prototype kernel-cost preflight (queue-sample + estimator) and a flag to short-circuit large batch admit (canary).
- Sam: implement conservative KV multiplier and smoothing window in admission logic, plus telemetry for kv_est per-request.
- Me (Anya): roll token_budget_target -20% to a 10-node canary and monitor reject rate, p95, and throughput.
- bench-bot/ci-bot: run regression tests that include synthetic KV-heavy traces.

ci-bot: queued test run: kv-heavy-workload/small-seqs x1000, will post results here when complete.

Kyle: One more thought — add a debug metric: admit_decision_reason -> {ok, kv_headroom_shrink, kernel_cost_shrink, preflight_blocked} so we can attribute why batches shrink/reject.

Anya: Great idea. If we can split rejects by reason we'll know whether to tune budgets or kernels.

Sam: Also note: when admitted batches are shrunk mid-flight there's extra Recompute pressure on kernels (cache churn) — metric: midflight_shrink_count. Let's surface that in Console so SREs can correlate with OOM events.

Anya: Will do. Plan: implement small changes as above, start canary today, sync back tomorrow with numbers. If anyone sees related alerts (prod-rt-4 cluster) ping me @Anya. :eyes:

Kyle: Thanks — I'll start the kernel preflight sketch now.

bench-bot: regression tests started (ETA ~22m).

Anya: Thanks all. Will update thread with canary dashboard link once up. :thumbsup:
